name: Smallest k such that Product_{i=1..k} (n+i) divides Product_{i=1..k} (n+k+i), or 0 if there is no such k.
comment: Erdős and Straus asked if a(n) exists for all n.

It can be shown that this is very similar to A375077, with the transformation (n, k) -> (n+k-1, n), though this doesn't guarantee minimality - a(7) here is much smaller than expected. - _Sharvil Kesarwani_, Mar 30 2026
link: Erdős problems database contributors, Erdős problem database, see no. 389.
Leandre Jack, Erdős Problem 389: the least k for n = 28 and n = 29, GitHub.
mathematica: Table[k = 1; While[Not[IntegerQ[Binomial[n + 2 k, k]/Binomial[n + k, n]]], k++]; k, {n, 0, 10}] (* _Vaclav Kotesovec_, Apr 01 2026 *)
program: (PARI) a(n) = my(k=1); while(prod(i=1, k, n+k+i)%prod(i=1, k, n+i), k++); k;
author: _Ralf Stephan_, Jul 29 2024
